title: On this day (Oct 12, 1928): the first iron lung
series: ON THIS DAY — daily, auto-researched by Lightpanda from Wikipedia:Selected_anniversaries/<Month_Day>

facts: 12 Oct 1928: the iron lung, a medical ventilator, was used for the first time, at Boston Children's Hospital, to treat an eight-year-old girl paralyzed by polio
Iron lungs work by negative pressure: changing air pressure around the body to draw air into the lungs
research.verify_before_posting: b5 claim: confirm that wild poliovirus is still endemic only in Pakistan and Afghanistan as of posting date (WHO / GPEI).

style_block: Mixed-media hand-cut PAPER COLLAGE, editorial zine style, theme 'atomic-age' 1920s-50s medical poster. Torn and scissor-cut paper edges, masking-tape corners, halftone print dots, old medical-journal clippings, real paper drop shadows. Figures are PRINTED-texture halftone cut-outs, not CGI, not a 3D render, keep print grain. Palette: hospital teal, cream, mustard, dark navy. Vertical 9:16 poster, flat scanned lighting. Keep the bottom quarter simple.

beats.script: In <1928,|nineteen twenty-eight,> || an eight-year-old girl || couldn't *breathe.* || So doctors put her || inside a *machine.*
*Polio* had paralyzed || the muscles she needed || to breathe.
The machine was a metal tank. || It changed the air pressure || around her body || and *pulled* air into her lungs.
October twelfth, <1928.|nineteen twenty-eight.> || The *iron* *lung* || was used for the first time.
Today, wild polio survives || in just *two* countries. || One of them... || is *Pakistan.*
Two drops of vaccine || do what the iron lung || never could. || *Give* the drops.

post.yt_title: They Put a Paralyzed Girl Inside a Machine (Oct 12, 1928)
post.ig_caption: 98 years ago today, an 8-year-old girl breathed again — inside a metal tank. Polio is almost gone. Almost. 💧💧
